# `css-modules/no-undefined-class`

**A CSS Module class that is read exists**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` (npm) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:css-modules/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (whether to add the class or fix the name is the author's call) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-css-modules/no-undef-class` |

## What it checks

`styles.name` reads a class the imported CSS Module defines. The finding is in the JavaScript or TypeScript file, at the name.

**Why:** reading a class the module does not define gives `undefined`, so the element silently loses its style; a typo or a renamed class shows up only on screen.

What the module defines counts `:export` keys and `@value` names, and the names `[css] modules_convention` makes reachable (`.btn-primary` is `styles.btnPrimary` under `camelCase`). A module whose class names the rule cannot work out (Sass interpolation, `&-suffix` on a selector list) is left alone, and so is a computed access such as `styles[name]`.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-css-modules
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:css-modules/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:css-modules/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"css-modules/no-undefined-class" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.js"]
rules = { "css-modules/no-undefined-class" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"css-modules/no-undefined-class" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"css-modules/no-undefined-class" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"css-modules/no-undefined-class" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "css-modules/no-undefined-class": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Also configured by `[css]`

CSS Modules: which stylesheets are modules, and how the bundler turns a class name into `styles.x`. Read by the `css-modules/*` rules and the project graph. Root config only.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `modules` | `array` | `[]` | Globs of CSS Module stylesheets besides `*.module.css` and `*.module.scss`, from the project root. |
| `modules_convention` | `asIs` · `camelCase` · `camelCaseOnly` · `dashes` · `dashesOnly` | `"asIs"` | css-loader's `localsConvention`: how a class such as `.btn-primary` is reached from JavaScript. `asIs`: `styles["btn-primary"]`; `camelCase`: that and `styles.btnPrimary`; `camelCaseOnly`: only `styles.btnPrimary`; `dashes` and `dashesOnly`: dashes become camel case, other characters stay. |

```toml
[css]
modules = ["src/**/*.styles.css"]
modules_convention = "camelCase"
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore css-modules/no-undefined-class: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore css-modules/no-undefined-class expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule css-modules/no-undefined-class --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain css-modules/no-undefined-class       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule css-modules/no-undefined-class  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                  # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Correct the name in the JavaScript or TypeScript file, or add the class to the module.
2. If the bundler maps names (`localsConvention`), set `[css] modules_convention` so the mapped names count.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.js
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card = styles.cards;
```

#### Do

```js files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.js
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card = styles.card;
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.cards} />;
```

#### Do

```jsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.ts
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card: string = styles["cards"];
```

#### Do

```ts files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.ts
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card: string = styles["card"];
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.tsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.cards} />;
```

#### Do

```tsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.tsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

## Differences from the source

eslint-plugin-css-modules's `no-undef-class` needs the stylesheet's path in each import; this rule follows the import through the project graph, and understands `[css] modules`, `composes`, `:export` and `@value`.
